name: Hammerhead
label: AmRep
lede: Three guys from Fargo, one guitar, one bass, one drum kit, and a run of records on Amphetamine Reptile that fans of the label still rank near the top of the catalog.

eras.title: Three outsiders from Fargo
eras.text: Paul Sanders, Paul Erickson and Jeff Mooridian Jr. started out in Fargo and Moorhead, then moved to Minneapolis. They found a home at Amphetamine Reptile Records before they had an album.

years.p: Hammerhead's first single on [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]]'s Amphetamine Reptile Records is the "Peep" 7". Wikipedia dates it to 1991.
years.xp:
The band came out of Fargo, North Dakota, where the trio first played together at a club called The Aquarium. Sanders told the Minneapolis paper City Pages that the band was never welcomed into the local hardcore scene.

Wikipedia lists "Peep" (1991) and "Load King" (1992) as their early 7" singles.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ethereal Killer · City Pages · Washington Post
years.h: Two days at Gark to make Ethereal Killer
years.p: Wikipedia says the band recorded their debut album in two days in October 1992 at Gark studio in Minneapolis. It runs ten songs in a bit under 33 minutes.
years.xp: Chris Coyne recorded and mixed it, with David B. Livingstone also credited. City Pages called it an unrelenting, rage-fueled debut, and the Washington Post heard real musicality under the noise, with Sanders and Erickson trading vocals and harmonizing.

eras.title: Records, road, and a tribute to Zen Arcade
eras.text: Two records in twelve months, a Husker Du cover, and a first major tour with Cows. This is the stretch fans mean when they say Hammerhead.

years.p: Ten songs, about 33 minutes, out on Amphetamine Reptile Records. AllMusic and Wikipedia date it 1993, though one AmRep fan site says 1992.

years.h: Hammerhead cover Husker Du for the Du Huskers tribute
years.p: Their track "Something I Learned Today" appears on the 1993 tribute Du Huskers, where Minnesota bands covered the whole of Zen Arcade.

years.h: First big tour: with Cows, the "loss of innocence tour"
years.p: Mooridian told City Pages that touring with [[Cows|d4b064a0-5567-4930-a359-16fadfa7941b]] was the band's first major tour, and called it the loss of innocence tour.
years.xp: The Cows were AmRep's Minneapolis noise-rock veterans. Mooridian gave the tour its nickname in a later City Pages interview, without saying which dates it covered.

years.p: The AmRep EP runs 18 minutes 42 seconds. Wikipedia says the tracks were recorded between 1991 and August 1993, so it doubles as a singles round-up.

years.src: Wikipedia: Into the Vortex · Portland Mercury · Seattle Times
years.h: Into the Vortex, cut in January at AmRep's own studio
years.p: Recorded by Tim Mac at Am Rep Recording Division in Minneapolis, with cover art by [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]]. The seven-minute "Journey to the Center of Tetnus 4" is the long one.
years.xp: The Portland Mercury called it one of the finest releases in AmRep's history. The Seattle Times said the songs explode like pop supernovas.
play: Journey to the Center of Tetnus 4

eras.title: Duh, the Big City and the exit
eras.text: A split single with Halo of Flies, a last album, and then Paul Sanders left for college. The trio ended in 1996.

years.h: "Camaro" with Kat Bjelland, on the Porn No. 1 split 7"
years.p: Babes in Toyland's Kat Bjelland sings on "Camaro", Hammerhead's side of a 1995 AmRep split 7" with [[Halo of Flies|3a26de45-4f41-4e28-bdc8-fda60ef0c8d0]]. It turned up again on the 1996 Screwed soundtrack.

years.h: Duh, the Big City is the last one
years.p: Eleven songs, recorded in 1995 at Beehive and Perma Sonics with Tim Mac. Erickson wrote most of it, Sanders wrote "Victoria" and the title track, and [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]] did the cover.

years.h: Sanders quits for a normal career
years.p: Paul Sanders left after Duh, the Big City to go to college and work. Nearly two decades later he called that decision a mistake.
years.xp:
In a 2014 interview with the Ice Planet blog, Sanders said he wanted a career and money for a while like a normal person, so he quit the band and went to college. He then played in Heroine Sheiks and Fly Republic and worked on More RAM.

Sources differ on timing: AllMusic and AmRep sites say he left in 1995, while Wikipedia and Sanders's own account put it after the 1996 album.

eras.title: Vaz, then back for more
eras.text: Paul Erickson and Jeff Mooridian Jr. moved into the duo Vaz. The original three came back in 2010.

years.p: After Hammerhead, bassist [[Paul Erickson|84245bbf-3baf-4f3a-be3b-217f62da5dd6]] and drummer [[Jeff Mooridian Jr.|b9f9930f-185f-419d-a8f2-5883cfcfe5ba]] formed [[Vaz|3edc106c-fb86-4c12-a616-5ebda994e399]], an experimental duo that later played on from New York.

years.src: Wikipedia: Janitor Joe · Ice Planet interview · AmRep A-Z (ihrtn.net)
years.p: Hammerhead played Amphetamine Reptile Records' 25th anniversary show in Minneapolis, then shows at Death By Audio in Brooklyn.
years.xp: Wikipedia's page on [[Janitor Joe|283d1035-e14b-45ee-a977-b533ea47cafc]] dates the anniversary night to August 29, 2010, and notes that Erickson also reformed that band for the same show. Sanders later said they only wanted to get back together if they could move the band forward.

years.h: Memory Hole EP, first new music in 15 years
years.p: The reunion produced an EP on Amphetamine Reptile Records in 2011. Sanders said recording across Brooklyn and Minneapolis was hard, but the band clicked again fast.
Wikipedia lists the reunion-era album New Directionz (2015) and a Learning Curve EP, Global Depression (2014).
